err-bc4.title: Printer Not Found (Win 11 RPC Block)
err-bc4.desc: Windows cannot find network shared printer on Windows 11 22H2/23H2/24H2.
err-bc4.rootCause: Windows 11 update changed default RPC policy to RPC over TCP, blocking legacy RPC over Named Pipes on port 445 SMB.
fixSteps: Enable RPC over Named Pipes policy in client Registry
Enable NTLM authentication fallback for IP connections (ForceKerberosForRpc = 0)
Restart Print Spooler service
Reconnect printer using network path: \\SERVER_IP\SHARE_NAME

err-bcb.title: Blocked Downloading Shared Printer Driver
err-bcb.desc: Cannot connect to printer due to Point and Print driver download restrictions.
err-bcb.rootCause: Windows Point and Print policy blocks standard users from downloading print drivers from untrusted servers.
fixSteps: Remove Admin-only driver installation restriction in Registry
Disable elevation prompt warning when installing Point and Print printer
Restart Spooler and reconnect to shared printer
err-bcb.riskNote: Allows standard users on local network to install shared printer drivers without Administrator privileges (softens Point and Print restrictions).

err-bc5.title: Untrusted Driver Package Blocked
err-bc5.desc: System blocked driver package installation from untrusted print server.
err-bc5.rootCause: Windows requires Point and Print servers to be explicitly whitelisted in Group Policy.
fixSteps: Download and install official driver locally on workstation first
Temporarily disable driver signature enforcement for modified drivers
Reconnect to shared printer once local driver is installed

err-bc6.title: Driver Architecture Mismatch (x86/x64)
err-bc6.desc: Print server lacks matching driver architecture for this workstation.
err-bc6.rootCause: The server does not share an additional 32-bit (x86) or 64-bit (x64) driver package compatible with client OS.
fixSteps: On Print Server, open Print Server Properties to add matching architecture driver
Or pre-install matching 64-bit/32-bit driver locally on workstation
Reconnect printer via network UNC path

err-bc7.title: Driver Package Signature Error
err-bc7.desc: Shared driver blocked due to revoked digital signature or expired WHQL certificate.
err-bc7.rootCause: Windows Driver Signature Enforcement blocks installing drivers with expired or untrusted catalog files.
fixSteps: Install WHQL-certified driver package
Import vendor root certificate into Trusted Publishers store
Restart Spooler and retry connection

err-bc8.title: Core Driver Dependency Installation Error
err-bc8.desc: Unable to install printer due to missing Windows Core Driver dependencies.
err-bc8.rootCause: Printer driver package relies on built-in Windows core print drivers (ntprint.inf) that are missing.
fixSteps: Restore built-in ntprint.inf core drivers from Windows Driver Store
Re-register Spooler system dependencies
Restart Print Spooler service

err-bcd.title: Point & Print Permission Blocked (User Restrict)
err-bcd.desc: Standard user lacks administrative privileges to install remote printer drivers.
err-bcd.rootCause: Microsoft security hardening mandates administrator approval for all Point and Print driver installs.
fixSteps: Configure RestrictDriverInstallationToAdministrators = 0
Set PointAndPrint PackagePointAndPrintServerList to trust local subnet
Restart Print Spooler service

err-bce.title: Print Server Security Certificate Conflict
err-bce.desc: RPC connection encryption between client and print server failed authentication.
err-bce.rootCause: Negotiation between Kerberos, NTLM, and RPC encryption failed on shared printer endpoint.
fixSteps: Configure RpcAuthentication = 0 on client
Synchronize system clocks between client and print server
Reconnect printer using IP address

err-11b.title: RPC Authentication Level Error (PrintNightmare)
err-11b.desc: Windows blocks shared printer connection due to RpcAuthnLevelPrivacyEnabled requirements.
err-11b.rootCause: PrintNightmare security patch mandates packet privacy encryption (RPC Level 6) on the Print Spooler server.
fixSteps: On Print Server, set RpcAuthnLevelPrivacyEnabled = 0 in Registry
Restart Print Spooler on Print Server
Reconnect printer from client workstation
err-11b.riskNote: Lowers RPC Privacy encryption level. Widely used by IT technicians and safe within trusted local network.

err-709.title: Cannot Connect to Printer (Error 0x709 - Client Side)
err-709.desc: Windows 10/11 client PC encounters error 0x00000709 when connecting to a network shared printer.
err-709.rootCause: Occurs when client connects to shared printer UNC path. Windows 11/10 default denies RPC over Named Pipes and fails Kerberos authentication over IP.
fixSteps: Enable RPC over Named Pipes policy (RpcUseNamedPipeProtocol = 1)
Disable Kerberos requirement for RPC over LAN (ForceKerberosForRpc = 0)
Enable LegacyDefaultPrinterMode = 1 in Registry
Restart Spooler and reconnect to printer

err-709-server.title: Win 11 Printer Sharing Error (Error 0x709 - Server Side)
err-709-server.desc: Win 11 Print Server blocks Win 10 client connections. Provides 2 options: Replace 3 DLL files or configure Registry.
err-709-server.rootCause: Windows 11 update changed default Spooler RPC listener to RPC over TCP only and disabled Named Pipes, preventing Windows 10 clients from connecting.
fixSteps: Option 1 (Replace 3 Spooler DLLs): Run once on server, auto backup to %ProgramData%\PrintLANFixer\backup_dll, all Win 10 clients can print immediately without client configuration.
Option 2 (Update Server Registry RpcProtocols = 7): Absolute safety, does not modify any Windows system files. Note: Each Win 10 client must run client script.
Restore original 3 files from backup folder anytime.

err-07c.title: Missing mscms.dll in Spool Directory
err-07c.desc: Issue caused by Windows security patch failing to load mscms.dll from server.
err-07c.rootCause: Windows Spooler cannot copy color management file mscms.dll from server driver store to client directory.
fixSteps: Copy mscms.dll from System32 into spool\drivers\x64\3 directory
Restart Print Spooler service
Reconnect shared printer

err-6ba.title: Print Spooler Stopped (RPC Server Unavailable)
err-6ba.desc: Workstation cannot connect to print server because RPC service is unavailable.
err-6ba.rootCause: Print Spooler (spoolsv.exe) service is stopped or port TCP 135/445 is blocked by firewall.
fixSteps: Start and configure Print Spooler service to Automatic
Verify RPC and DCOM Server services are running
Verify TCP port 135 and 445 on print server

err-6d9.title: Windows Firewall Blocking Printer Sharing
err-6d9.desc: Cannot enable printer sharing because Windows Firewall service is disabled or blocked.
err-6d9.rootCause: Windows Firewall (MpsSvc) service must be running and File & Printer Sharing rules enabled.
fixSteps: Start Windows Firewall service (MpsSvc)
Enable File and Printer Sharing rules in Windows Firewall
Enable Network Discovery rule group

err-6be.title: RPC Call Failed (Spooler Crash)
err-6be.desc: Print Spooler process crashed abruptly during remote procedure call.
err-6be.rootCause: Corrupted print processor or buggy third-party print monitor caused spoolsv.exe to crash.
fixSteps: Terminate hung spoolsv.exe process
Purge corrupted spool queue files in C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS
Restart Print Spooler service

err-4005.title: Unspecified Error Connecting to Shared Printer
err-4005.desc: Windows encountered an unspecified error connecting to shared printer network path.
err-4005.rootCause: Network discovery, SMBv2/v3 signing, or workgroup communication is misconfigured between PCs.
fixSteps: Enable Network Discovery and File and Printer Sharing in Network Settings
Verify Workgroup or Domain name consistency between machines
Test connectivity to host via ping and UNC path: \\SERVER_IP

err-005.title: Access Denied to Shared Printer
err-005.desc: User account lacks permission to connect or print on target host.
err-005.rootCause: Sharing permissions or NTFS security on print server does not allow Everyone or Guest account access.
fixSteps: On Print Server, set Printer Security permissions to allow "Everyone" Print permission
Configure Share Permissions to allow Everyone Full Control
Enable Insecure Guest Authentication if connecting without password

err-52e.title: Logon Failure (Invalid Credentials)
err-52e.desc: Saved username or password in Windows Credential Manager is incorrect or expired.
err-52e.rootCause: Host PC changed account password or client cached obsolete network credentials.
fixSteps: Open Windows Credential Manager (control keymgr.dll)
Remove outdated stored Windows Credentials for the print server
Add new Windows Credential with correct host username and password

err-35.title: Network Path Not Found
err-35.desc: The network path was not found when browsing printer host IP or hostname.
err-35.rootCause: NetBIOS name resolution failed, host PC is unreachable, or subnet mask is mismatched.
fixSteps: Verify host PC is powered on and connected to the same LAN or subnet
Verify host IP address and ping from client
Enable SMBv1/v2/v3 client protocol if communicating with legacy server

err-040.title: Network Name No Longer Available
err-040.desc: Network communication interrupted or SMB session terminated abruptly.
err-040.rootCause: Network card sleep mode, SMB session timeout, or unstable Wi-Fi/switch port disconnected printer link.
fixSteps: Disable network adapter Power Saving mode (Allow computer to turn off this device)
Verify network cable or Wi-Fi link stability
Restart Print Spooler on both client and host

err-3e3.title: I/O Operation Aborted (Timeout)
err-3e3.desc: Print operation was aborted because print server did not respond in time.
err-3e3.rootCause: Large print spool file timeout or corrupted temporary spool files blocking the queue.
fixSteps: Pause Print Spooler and purge huge stuck spool files
Increase Spooler timeout threshold in Registry
Restart Spooler and re-submit print job

err-07e.title: The Specified Module Could Not Be Found
err-07e.desc: System failed to find specific printer driver DLL module in Spool directory.
err-07e.rootCause: Driver files were partially copied or corrupted during network driver installation.
fixSteps: Reinstall printer driver package with admin privileges
Verify that driver DLL files are present in spool\drivers folder
Restart Print Spooler

err-057.title: Invalid Parameter in Printer Configuration
err-057.desc: Printer port or Registry settings contain invalid parameters or corrupt entries.
err-057.rootCause: Printer registry keys in HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print contain invalid values.
fixSteps: Check printer port mapping in Print Server Properties
Reconfigure TCP/IP port with correct IP address and Raw 9100 port
Remove invalid registry keys under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print\Printers

err-bbb.title: Printer Port Does Not Exist
err-bbb.desc: The printer points to a TCP/IP port or USB endpoint that no longer exists.
err-bbb.rootCause: Printer IP address changed via DHCP or physical USB port changed without remapping.
fixSteps: Verify physical printer USB connection or network IP address
Reconfigure printer port in Printer Properties > Ports
Restart Print Spooler

err-canon-comm.title: Canon LBP 2900 / 3300 Communication Error
err-canon-comm.desc: Canon printer displays "Communication Error" over network sharing or USB.
err-canon-comm.rootCause: Conflict between Canon CAPT background monitor and virtual network ports (CNBJNP).
fixSteps: Delete conflicting USB Monitor registry keys
Scan and remove legacy CNBJNP network monitors
Copy mscms.dll color module to driver folder
Restart Print Spooler and re-plug printer USB cable

err-wpp-win11.title: Windows 11 24H2 Blocks Legacy v3/v4 Drivers
err-wpp-win11.desc: Windows Protected Print (WPP) blocks third-party printer drivers completely.
err-wpp-win11.rootCause: Windows 11 24H2 activates WPP by default, forcing Mopria/IPP mode and blocking standard INF drivers.
fixSteps: Disable Windows Protected Print mode via Registry / Group Policy
Restart Print Spooler service
Install vendor printer driver package (V3 / V4 INF)

err-spooler-crash.title: Print Spooler Crashes Repeatedly on Startup
err-spooler-crash.desc: spoolsv.exe crashes immediately on launch due to corrupt driver files.
err-spooler-crash.rootCause: Corrupt 64-bit or 32-bit printer driver binary in spool\drivers folder triggers access violation.
fixSteps: Isolate corrupted driver folder (rename x64 to x64.old)
Clear all pending queue files in spool\PRINTERS
Restart Print Spooler service to rebuild clean environment

util-canon-comm-fix.title: Fix Canon LBP 2900 / 3300 Communication Error
util-canon-comm-fix.desc: Resolve Canon communication failure caused by CNBJNP and USB Monitor conflicts.
stepTitles: Stop Print Spooler and purge pending queue files

aboutModal.title: Application Information
aboutModal.subtitle: PrintLAN Fixer - LAN Printer Diagnostic & Troubleshooting Utility
aboutModal.appIntro: PrintLAN Fixer is a high-performance standalone desktop utility built to resolve classic Windows network printing errors (0x00000709, 0x0000011b, 0x00000bc4, Canon Spooler deadlocks, Point & Print blocks, etc.).
aboutModal.preCheck1: It is strongly recommended to create a System Restore Point or backup the Registry before applying deep system modifications (such as Spooler DLL replacements).
aboutModal.preCheck2: Double-check the server IP address/hostname and physical network connection before diagnosing software issues.
aboutModal.preCheck3: Carefully review the technical explanation and execution script in the 'Details' view prior to clicking 'Fix'.
aboutModal.disclaimerP1: PrintLAN Fixer directly modifies Windows Registry settings, Print Spooler service configurations, system DLL files, and Windows Firewall rules.
aboutModal.disclaimerP2: This tool is provided 'AS-IS' for technical community and IT Helpdesk support without warranty of any kind. The author assumes NO liability for any system disruption, software conflicts, or data loss arising from using this software.
aboutModal.disclaimerP3: Users must possess basic Windows networking knowledge and take full responsibility when running on production or critical print servers.
aboutModal.feedbackDesc: All bug reports, feature suggestions, or requests for supporting custom printer errors are welcomed on the project's GitHub Issues page.
aboutModal.feedbackGuide1: Specify your Windows OS build (e.g., Windows 11 24H2 or Windows 10 22H2).
aboutModal.feedbackGuide2: Include the exact error code (0x00000709, 0x0000011b...) and printer model (Canon LBP 2900, HP LaserJet, Brother...).
aboutModal.feedbackGuide3: Clarify the machine role (Server host with USB cable or Client workstation over LAN).
aboutModal.donateDesc: If PrintLAN Fixer saved you time and resolved your printing headaches, a cup of coffee would be greatly appreciated to keep this project actively maintained! ☕
